ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a larger circle in the figure, with the internal shaded area gray; inside the large circle there are seven identical small white circles, one of which is at the center, and the other six are arranged around the central small circle. The six outer small circles are respectively tangent to the central small circle, and adjacent outer small circles are tangent to each other; at the same time, they are also tangent to the large circle. Reasoning: The radius of each small circle is 1. The central small circle is tangent to any outer small circle, so the distance from the center of the central small circle to the center of an outer small circle is 1+1=2. From the sixfold symmetric arrangement in the figure, it can be known that the large circle and the central small circle are concentric. The outer small circles are internally tangent to the large circle, therefore the radius of the large circle equals the distance from the center to the center of an outer small circle plus the radius of the small circle, that is, 2+1=3. The shaded area equals the area of the large circle minus the areas of the seven small circles: π·3^2−7·π·1^2=9π−7π=2π.

By the sixfold symmetric arrangement visible in the image, the large circle has the same center as the central small circle. Since each surrounding circle is internally tangent to the large circle, the large circle radius is 2+1=3. Compute shaded area as area of the large disk minus the areas of the seven small disks: 9π−7π=2π.

method.method_draft: Exploit the sixfold symmetry shown in the image by dividing the large circle into six congruent 60-degree sectors using radii from the common center through the centers of the six surrounding circles. From the text, adjacent small circles and the central circle are all tangent with radius 1, so the triangle formed by the central center and two adjacent surrounding centers has side lengths 2,2,2; hence each sector angle is 60 degrees. The large radius is 3 because a surrounding circle center is 2 units from the central center and its radius is 1. In one 60-degree sector, the large-sector area is (1/6)·9π=3π/2. The unshaded small-circle area inside that sector consists of one sixth of the central unit circle plus two half-disks from the adjacent surrounding unit circles, totaling π/6+π. Thus the shaded area in one sector is 3π/2−π−π/6=π/3, and multiplying by 6 gives 2π.
